title: Local AI Agent (Human-in-the-Loop)
tagline: Desktop agent with a local LLM and mandatory human approval
problem: Designed an AI agent to run 100% on the local machine — no paid API, no data leaving the computer — under one central safety constraint: a local model must never be allowed to write files or run commands on its own.
targetUser: Personal use (the data scope explicitly excludes any work-related content).
myRole: Sole developer: desktop app, Rust backend, LLM integration.
process: Built a Tauri 2 (Rust) + React + TypeScript desktop app with a local LLM via Ollama, applying TDD on the Rust backend — sandbox, agenda and audit modules each have their own test suites. The model answers with a "structured intent" (JSON carrying the proposed action: write file, read, run command) that enters an approval queue with a diff before anything executes.
keyDecisions: Non-negotiable human-in-the-loop: the model only proposes; every execution goes through Approve/Reject. No autonomous mode, visible or hidden.
Tauri over Electron: real declarative sandboxing — the frontend never touches the filesystem or processes directly, only through exposed Rust commands.
File sandbox with canonicalize() and a workspace prefix check, tested against path traversal, absolute paths and new files.
Terminal sandbox limits documented honestly: cwd pinned to the workspace, but the effective defense is manual approval of the exact command.
Append-only audit log (JSONL), tolerant to corrupted lines.
result: Working agent: chat with a local model, approval queue with diffs, sandboxed file and terminal execution, conversation history, a personal checklist agenda and an action-reports view — fully offline.
learned: Rust and Tauri in depth: capabilities, tests and defensive parsing — local models occasionally wrap JSON in code fences and the parser must tolerate it. An agent's safety architecture is a product decision, not an implementation detail: proposing ≠ executing, and that boundary must live in the runtime, not in the prompt.
